solution: As in the easy version, after the last assignment with base x the cell's value is always x, -x or 0: negation flips the sign, and clamping is a no-op on a non-negative value but kills a negative one to 0 for the rest of the epoch. With values up to 1e9 a lazy tag can no longer tabulate every possible incoming value, so exploit that factorisation: the values a tag appends before its own first assignment are |v| times a +1/-1/0 pattern that depends only on the sign of the incoming value v, and everything from that first assignment onward is a fixed concrete sequence. A tag therefore stores two sign-branch max-subarray tuples (sum, prefix, suffix, best) as coefficients of |v|, the outgoing sign for each branch (0 encodes the dead-at-zero state), and one concrete tuple plus outgoing value for the part after its first assignment; all four components scale linearly in |v| >= 0, so the max operations inside a Kadane merge never mix scaled with unscaled terms and composition of two tags stays O(1). Feed these tags to a lazy segment tree over positions: updates are the usual O(log n), and a query pushes the path down, materialises the leaf's concrete tuple, then appends a run of the current value up to the query time and reports the best field. The lastans encoding forces the whole thing online. Total O((n + q) log n) time, O(n) memory.

notes: Verified: brute force plus a full implementation of the tag algebra and the lazy segment tree above; both reproduce the official sample exactly and agree on 4400 random general-value tests (plus a 20000-case stress of the tag algebra alone against a direct simulation, checking the max-subarray value, the outgoing value and the covered length), with internal invariants asserted. The statement is complete, not truncated. On the version pair: E1 and E2 share the architecture (lazy segment tree, lazy tag = composable summary of a block of operations, Kadane merge at the leaf), so the overlapping labels are real and not a labelling failure. The genuine difference is the tag's representation: E1 can brute-force a lookup table over the only three possible cell values, which is why E1 carries 'brute-force' and E2 does not; E2 must instead observe that the value is always +/-|base| or 0 and represent the tag as a sign-branched function that is linear in the magnitude, with a separate concrete part after its first assignment. That is the 500-point gap, and it is an algebra insight rather than a new data structure, which is why the judge tags E2 with data structures alone. Vocabulary gaps, same as E1: no 'kadane' / 'maximum-subarray-sum' label (used 'dynamic-programming' as the closest), and nothing for 'composable lazy tag / operation monoid' or 'forced online'. Deliberately NOT labelled offline-queries or persistent-segment-tree - the 'versions' in the statement are a read-only history, not a persistence requirement.
